subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Eagle and Divine Power
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Eagle and Divine Power usable.

hook.text: Zeus sent an eagle to eat Prometheus's liver. Rome's legions carried eagle standards. The bird means empire.

buildup.text: Eagles fly higher than any other bird. They see everything from above. Height became a metaphor for authority.

discovery.text: The Aztec empire began where an eagle sat on a cactus eating a snake. Mexico's flag still carries this image.

twist.text: America chose the bald eagle. Nazi Germany used the eagle. Both claimed divine authority through the same bird.

climax.text: The eagle is the most political animal in myth. It doesn't just represent power—it legitimizes it.

punchline.text: Fly highest. See farthest. Rule everything.

quiz.question: Why did the Aztecs found their capital where they did?
options: An eagle sat on a cactus eating a snake
